response.reason: NL1 is purely descriptive scope-setting (names the domain: UAV swarm state machine) and carries no independently violable obligation, so it is marked context. NL2 establishes (a) a continuous/repeated target-search task obligation before mission completion (state_action), and (b) a cardinality obligation that the swarm operates within exactly three distinct state areas (cardinality, member_domain=concurrent_regions is not established explicitly as parallel regions; the text says 'three different state areas' which most naturally reads as three named/enumerable operating states, so explicit_named_members/direct_child_states is preferred over concurrent_regions since no parallel/orthogonal semantics is stated - selected direct_child_states as primary with explicit_named_members as alternative). NL3 establishes a transition endpoint from an interception condition to the 'formation adjustment' state, with 'intercepted' as the triggering event on that alternative. NL4 establishes: (i) a transition endpoint into the 'attack' state guarded/triggered by receipt of task assignment information during flight, (ii) a termination-like completion of the attack activity ('after completing the attack') which reduces UAV count - modeled as a variable_delta effect contract on the swarm-size variable, tied to the attack state's exit/completion. The attack completion is not itself a NamedCompletionState of the whole mission (mission completion is referenced in NL2 as a separate future condition), so it is kept as a state_action/variable_delta obligation rather than a termination contract for the whole system. Transition groups capture the shared-source relations: an implicit target-search/patrol source transitioning to formation-adjustment (on intercepted) and to attack (on task assignment during flight) as two alternatives from the same continuing 'search' operating context, since both NL3 and NL4 describe conditions arising during the ongoing search activity described in NL2. No explicit initial-entry or containment owner is named beyond the three state areas, so initial_entry/containment contracts are limited to what NL2 supports: the three areas are children of the overall UAV swarm system, and search/target-search is the initial default operating state entered before interception or task assignment can occur (implied by 'before mission completed, continuously performs target search... during which it operates within three state areas' and the subsequent 'when intercepted' / 'during flight, if...' clauses that presuppose the swarm is already in the search/flight state). I preserve this as initial_entry into the search-task state under the swarm-system owner in NL2, and containment of the three state areas under that same owner.

stage_receipts.reason: NL1 is purely descriptive scope-setting (names the domain: UAV swarm state machine) and carries no independently violable obligation, so it is marked context. NL2 establishes (a) a continuous/repeated target-search task obligation before mission completion (state_action), and (b) a cardinality obligation that the swarm operates within exactly three distinct state areas (cardinality, member_domain=concurrent_regions is not established explicitly as parallel regions; the text says 'three different state areas' which most naturally reads as three named/enumerable operating states, so explicit_named_members/direct_child_states is preferred over concurrent_regions since no parallel/orthogonal semantics is stated - selected direct_child_states as primary with explicit_named_members as alternative). NL3 establishes a transition endpoint from an interception condition to the 'formation adjustment' state, with 'intercepted' as the triggering event on that alternative. NL4 establishes: (i) a transition endpoint into the 'attack' state guarded/triggered by receipt of task assignment information during flight, (ii) a termination-like completion of the attack activity ('after completing the attack') which reduces UAV count - modeled as a variable_delta effect contract on the swarm-size variable, tied to the attack state's exit/completion. The attack completion is not itself a NamedCompletionState of the whole mission (mission completion is referenced in NL2 as a separate future condition), so it is kept as a state_action/variable_delta obligation rather than a termination contract for the whole system. Transition groups capture the shared-source relations: an implicit target-search/patrol source transitioning to formation-adjustment (on intercepted) and to attack (on task assignment during flight) as two alternatives from the same continuing 'search' operating context, since both NL3 and NL4 describe conditions arising during the ongoing search activity described in NL2. No explicit initial-entry or containment owner is named beyond the three state areas, so initial_entry/containment contracts are limited to what NL2 supports: the three areas are children of the overall UAV swarm system, and search/target-search is the initial default operating state entered before interception or task assignment can occur (implied by 'before mission completed, continuously performs target search... during which it operates within three state areas' and the subsequent 'when intercepted' / 'during flight, if...' clauses that presuppose the swarm is already in the search/flight state). I preserve this as initial_entry into the search-task state under the swarm-system owner in NL2, and containment of the three state areas under that same owner.
